clue.text: Disorder when the Queen joins the volunteers?

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: joins here means enters the ranks of, so the monarch goes inside the volunteers

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
HM stands for Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about what ailment arises when the monarch enlists in the reserves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joins' reads as a link but is the container signal. The Territorial Army is the British army's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthma is a respiratory complaint, an example of a medical disorder.

clue.text: No end of vulgar language on the boat

indicators.note: having no end means the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: argot is slang, the coarse jargon of a group

explanation.surface: A ship where the crew swear nonstop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' looks like 'plenty of', but it trims the last letter from ARGOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the legendary ship of Jason and his Argonauts.

clue.text: Shoot with a 10-bore, almost

parts.note: the number ten written out as a word

indicators.note: almost means the synonym stops one letter short of complete

parts.note: to bore a hole is to drill it

explanation.surface: Firing a shotgun that is nearly a ten-bore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' and '10-bore' suggest guns; shoot is a plant's growth, and bore is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is a slender climbing growth, a kind of plant shoot.

clue.text: Boss lady and compiler writing to a hospital from the same source

parts.note: the setter of the crossword refers to themself as me
MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
ib. is short for ibidem, used in citations for the same source

explanation.surface: A female manager and the crossword setter write to a hospital, quoting the same reference.
explanation.walkthrough: MEMSAHIB was the term in colonial India for a European woman of rank, the mistress of a household.
explanation.definitionFit: A memsahib was the mistress of a household in colonial India, a woman in charge.

clue.text: Armistice cut short and broken by the sword

indicators.note: broken signals that the letters are smashed and rearranged
cut short means the last letter of the word is lopped off

explanation.surface: A peace truce is ended abruptly and shattered by a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes E off Armistice, leaving ARMISTIC; 'broken' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A scimitar is a curved oriental sword, an example of the weapon.

clue.text: Ruler of roost given food, containing caper, on plate

indicators.note: containing means one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: cheer can mean food and drink, as in good cheer

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: an antic is a playful caper or prank
L is the letter shown on a learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: Someone is fed and dances about on a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' splits the food word after its second letter. In the UK a learner driver displays an L-plate, so plate gives L.
explanation.definitionFit: Chanticleer is the traditional name of the cockerel in fables, the bird who rules the roost.

clue.text: Sheep, none too bright, raised by diminutive character

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the whole run is read upwards

parts.note: a teg is a sheep in its second year
dim means not very clever or not very luminous

explanation.surface: A small person lifts a dull-witted sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns TEGDIM upwards. A TEG is a two-year-old sheep, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A midget is a very small person, so a diminutive character fits.

clue.text: Tax Officer admits heavenly creature's a hybrid

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: T is an abbreviation for tax
O is an abbreviation for officer
an angel is a heavenly being; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A taxman lets in an angel who turns out to be a cross-breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' puts ANGEL between T and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a citrus fruit bred by crossing a tangerine with a pomelo or grapefruit.

clue.text: City seized by strange inclination when lying down

indicators.note: seized by means held inside the other piece

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
EC is the postcode for the City of London
a bent is a natural inclination or tendency

explanation.surface: A city is gripped by an odd tendency to lie about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seized by' is the container signal. Strange meaning rum is British slang, and the City of London has its own postcode letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Recumbent describes a person reclining or lying flat.

clue.text: 6 taking drug for the secret of life

indicators.note: taking means letting the other piece inside

parts.note: the answer at 6 down is a small person, and so is a gnome
E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A small figure takes drugs in search of the meaning of life.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 6 points at a small person, here a GNOME, which takes E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The full DNA sequence of an organism holds the genetic code, poetically the secret of life.

clue.text: Fellow in woman's clothing, cold and contemptuous

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a sari is a garment worn by women in South Asia
a don is a fellow of a university college
C stands for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A man in a dress is chilly and scornful.
explanation.walkthrough: A university fellow is a DON, a British academic term.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardonic means grimly mocking or scornful, close to contemptuous.

clue.text: Spotlit woman with a lot behind her?

parts.note: broad is old American slang for a woman
lit by a spotlight means caught in its beam of light

explanation.surface: A woman in a spotlight who has a big backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotlit' comes first but supplies the end of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad in the beam is an idiom for having wide hips or a large bottom.

clue.text: One hungry to absorb Scripture into the bloodstream

indicators.note: to absorb means to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
ravenous means extremely hungry
NT is the New Testament, part of the Scriptures

explanation.surface: A starving person eagerly takes in holy texts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorb' is the container signal, with the scriptural abbreviation going in right after the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Intravenous means delivered into a vein, so straight into the bloodstream.

clue.text: Heraldic flower in north European state leader's time and motion study

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: Baltic describes the countries around the Baltic Sea in northern Europe
lis is the fleur-de-lis, a stylised lily in heraldry

indicators.note: a leader is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A lily in a Baltic nation's leader's efficiency study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time and motion study' sounds like workplace efficiency analysis, but it describes the science of moving projectiles.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballistics studies the flight of projectiles, tracking their motion over time.

clue.text: Boycotts narcotic in dangerous location

parts.note: to black something is to boycott it, as unions do with goods
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone shuns drugs found in a risky place.
explanation.walkthrough: To black goods is British trade-union usage for boycotting them.
explanation.definitionFit: A black spot is a place known for accidents or danger, such as on a road.

clue.text: Peacemaker took the plunge across the water

definitions.meaning: a politician favouring peace, and a symbol of peace

definitions.text: took the plunge across the water
definitions.meaning: in American English the past tense of dive is ...; across the water means in the US

explanation.surface: A peacemaker swam across the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird symbol of peace, and the American past tense of dive.

clue.text: Ooze conceals sort of beauty, they say

indicators.note: conceals means hides the other piece within it

parts.note: to seep is to ooze slowly
a kind is a sort or type

explanation.surface: A trickle hides a certain kind of beauty, as people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' looks like a sound signal; it points to the saying that beauty is only skin-deep.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that beauty is only superficial, lying on the surface.

clue.text: Elderly artist not quite making a comeback

indicators.note: coming back means the letters are read in the reverse direction
not quite means the name stops one letter short

parts.note: Edgar Degas was a French Impressionist painter

explanation.surface: An old painter is not quite returning to form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims DEGAS to DEGA; 'making a comeback' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged is a direct synonym for old, as in elderly.

clue.text: Letter from Spain gets left near the bottom of the slope

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

indicators.note: near the bottom means inserted close to the end of the other word

parts.note: a piste is a ski slope

explanation.surface: A message from Spain arrives at the foot of a ski run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near the bottom of' puts L just before the final E of PISTE.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal letter, as in the New Testament epistles.

clue.text: As a Turk, rue sorting out Germany's pickle

indicators.note: sorting out means rearranging the letters

explanation.surface: A Turkish man regrets having to deal with Germany's tricky situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickle' suggests a predicament, but here it is the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauerkraut is pickled shredded cabbage, a German speciality.

clue.text: Mostly tropical mixed fruit

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are jumbled
mostly means all but the last letter

explanation.surface: A mix of mostly tropical fruits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops L, leaving TROPICA, which 'mixed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The apricot is a stone fruit, an example of fruit.

clue.text: Silence in jail!

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both be quiet and confined behind bars.

clue.text: Make a mistake in thanking misguided attempt at quixotic behaviour

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece
misguided signals that the letters go astray into a new order

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Botching your thanks is a misguided Don Quixote-style gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misguided' rearranges the letters of thanking into KNIGHTAN, and 'in' splits that after its sixth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Quixote styled himself a wandering knight seeking adventure, so his chivalric antics are this.

clue.text: Beat departed spirit

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died, departed
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Defeating a ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests a ghost; it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To drum is to beat rhythmically.

clue.text: Drink made of vegetable containing iodine and nitrogen

indicators.note: containing means holding the other piece within

parts.note: a potato is a vegetable
I is the chemical symbol for iodine
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A drink distilled from a vegetable with added chemical elements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' places I just before the last O of POTATO.
explanation.definitionFit: A potation is an archaic word for a drink, especially an alcoholic one.

clue.text: Left vehicle in northern town

parts.note: red describes the political left
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A car abandoned in a town up north.
explanation.walkthrough: REDCAR is a seaside town in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcar is a coastal town in the north of England.

clue.text: Forbidden incursion of hair into the bath? Just the opposite

indicators.note: into normally means the first piece goes inside the second
just the opposite swaps the roles, so the bath goes inside the hair

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair
Bath is a spa town, and a spa is a bath

explanation.surface: A hair in the bath is an unwelcome intrusion, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' alone would put hair inside the bath; 'Just the opposite' flips the roles, so the bath goes inside the hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Trespass is unlawful entry onto property, an incursion that is not allowed.

clue.text: What's emitted by Greek character leading sheep westward

indicators.note: in an across clue, westward means read from right to left
leading means the first piece goes in front

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
tups are rams, male sheep

explanation.surface: A Greek man drives his sheep towards the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'westward' turns round the whole run, so the Greek letter ends up at the end of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sputum is spittle or phlegm, matter coughed out of the body.
